item.title: Scottish Premiership: Durán caps Celtic’s comeback win over Hibs
item.description: Hibernian 1-2 Celtic; Rangers 4-0 St Johnstone Kevin Kelsy scores two to sink 10-man Saints Camilo Durán moved into double figures for the season as Celtic reasserted themselves at the top of the Premiership by coming from behind to defeat beleaguered Hibernian 2-1 at windy Easter Road. After another Europa League setback at home to Celta Vigo on Thursday, the champions bounced back with a victory that restored their four-point cushion over Rangers at the top. The home side, who are bottom, took an early lead through Owen Elding but it was swiftly cancelled out by a Jason Kerr own goal before Duran’s 10th of the season edged the visitors ahead just before the break. item.title: Arch Manning has another viral moment with ESPN's Holly Rowe
item.description: Arch Manning has another viral moment with ESPN's Holly Rowe originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Arch Manning's roller coaster season continued on Saturday night, when Texas took down Ole Miss in a crucial game. This game was at the center of the college football world, as ABC sent its top team to Austin to broadcast the game. That included sideline reporter Holly Rowe, who was involved in a controversy regarding Texas from earlier in the season. After Texas beat Ohio State, head coach Steve Sarkisian blew off Rowe postgame while Manning admitted to laughing at an AI video of Sarkisian slapping Rowe. Both Sarkisian and Manning apologized for their sides of the controversy, and it seems like the relationship between them and Rowe is in a good place. When Manning spoke with Rowe following the Longhorns' win Saturday night, he joked with Rowe that he'd love for her to work more Texas games in the future. Here's why he said that. MORE : Arch Manning, Texas barely save soap opera season with thrilling Ole Miss victory Why Arch Manning wants Holly Rowe at more Texas games After Arch Manning led Texas to a big win over Ole Miss on Saturday night, the quarterback participated in the standard postgame interview with ESPN's Holly Rowe. At the very end, Manning told Rowe he'd like her to cover more Texas games. "You need to start doing our games more," Manning said. "We're 3-0 with you this year." "Whatever it takes." 😤 Arch Manning and @TexasFootball get a BIG win over No. 7 Ole Miss 🔥 https://t.co/WxPMYFtlbE — SEC Network (@SECNetwork) October 25, 2026 Manning is not wrong with his analysis. Texas has now beaten Ohio State, Tennessee, and Ole Miss with ABC's top team broadcasting their games, which includes Holly Rowe on the sidelines while Chris Fowler and Kirk Herbstreit are in the booth. As long as Texas keeps winning games, they will draw ABC's No. 1 team during select games. That would especially be the case if the Longhorns make the College Football Playoff, as no broadcast team does more Playoff games than Fowler, Herbstreit, and Rowe. item.title: Grêmio fans charter 40 coaches and will pack the away end
item.description: Grêmio fans charter 40 coaches and will pack the away end If it were up to the fans alone, Grêmio would be fighting for the title or, at the very least, a Libertadores spot in the 2026 Brasileirão. The match against Coritiba on Monday (26) is another example of that. There will be 40 BUSES full of fans heading to Curitiba. Around 12,000 fans signed up to travel on the buses provided by the club—Grêmio had to select who would go. And this is just one more example of the Grêmio fans’ love for their club. Despite sitting just 18th in the Brasileirão, Grêmio ranks FOURTH in attendance. Grêmio averages 30,657 fans per game, behind only Flamengo (59,928), Corinthians (37,860), and Bahia (34,664). With this support behind them, Grêmio will try to turn things around and stay in Série A. With 31 points, Grêmio is four points behind Inter, who have 35 and have already played this round. item.title: Preview | Lecce vs Juventus
item.description: Preview | Lecce vs Juventus The Men's First Team are back in Serie A action, this time heading south to face Lecce in Puglia. The Serie A Matchday 8 clash is set to take place at the Stadio Via del Mare at 18:00 CET on Sunday, October 25. Let’s get up to speed ahead of Sunday's game with some pre-match stats. INTERESTING FACTS HEADED GOALS – Juventus have scored four of their nine Serie A goals this season with headers, accounting for 44% of their total. Across Europe's top five leagues, only Lecce have a higher percentage, with five headed goals out of nine (56%). KOLO MUANI ON THE ROAD – Six of Randal Kolo Muani's nine Serie A goals for Juventus have come away from home (67%). The French forward has also been directly involved in a goal in each of his last two league away appearances, providing an assist against Sassuolo and scoring against Cagliari. CLOSING IN ON DOUBLE FIGURES – With nine Serie A goals to his name, Randal Kolo Muani is just one away from reaching double figures for Juventus. He could become the sixth French player to achieve this milestone for the Bianconeri in the competition. BALL POSSESSION – Juventus rank fourth in Serie A for average possession this season (58.7%), behind Inter, Como and Milan. UNDER PRESSURE – Only Inter (3,232) have faced more opposition pressures than Juventus (3,179) in Serie A this season. OPPOSITION FOCUS LECCE'S FORM – Eusebio Di Francesco's side come into the match following a 3-0 away win over Udinese, with goals from Kialonda Gaspar, Konan N'Dri and Jamil Siebert. Lecce have recorded three wins and four defeats in their opening seven league matches, without drawing a game. AERIAL THREAT – Lecce have scored five of their nine Serie A goals this season with headers (56%), the highest proportion of any team across Europe's top five leagues. TIAGO GABRIEL'S IMPACT – The 2004-born defender has been directly involved in three goals in six Serie A appearances this season, scoring twice and providing one assist. Since the start of last season, no defender born in 2004 or later has scored more Serie A goals than Tiago Gabriel (four). DANILO VEIGA'S ASSISTS – The Lecce defender has registered two assists in seven league appearances this season, both coming in his side's last two home matches against Monza and Bologna. That is already twice as many as he managed in his previous 49 Serie A appearances combined (one). HIGH PRESSING – Lecce have applied more pressures to their opponents than any other Serie A side this season (3,129), despite recording the lowest average possession in the competition (39.8%).

item.description: Barcelona face fresh PSG threat in race to sign wantaway Manchester United wonderkid – report Barcelona face a growing challenge in their pursuit of Manchester United teenager JJ Gabriel, with Paris Saint-Germain stepping up their efforts to secure the highly rated youngster. According to a report from SPORT , PSG have opened talks with the 16-year-old’s representatives, adding another complication to a transfer battle that also involves Real Madrid. For Barça , signing the young talent is going to be a significant test of their ability to attract one of England’s most promising young attacking talents. It is said that Gabriel is drawn to Barcelona’s footballing philosophy and record of developing young players, but that preference alone may not be enough to secure his signature. PSG increase pressure on Barcelona in JJ Gabriel race As per the outlet, PSG are looking to take advantage of the uncertainty surrounding Gabriel’s future at Old Trafford by presenting an appealing sporting and financial proposal. PSG have entered the race for JJ Gabriel. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) Real Madrid are also pushing to strengthen their case, leaving Barcelona facing competition from two clubs capable of offering substantial financial incentives. Recent reporting has identified Real Madrid and PSG as serious contenders, with discussions involving Gabriel’s representatives already under way, although it is crucial to note that the teenager’s final decision is pending. Barcelona’s sporting project could prove decisive Gabriel is understood to have a particular affinity for Barcelona, whose emphasis on technical football and youth development could appeal to a player seeking a pathway towards senior professional football. La Masia’s reputation remains an important part of the club’s attraction for emerging talents. However, Barcelona cannot assume that their sporting philosophy will automatically outweigh rival offers, particularly if PSG and Real Madrid are prepared to provide more lucrative terms. JJ Gabriel is attracted to Barcelona. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) The club is reportedly unwilling to enter an expensive bidding war for a player who has yet to make his official first-team debut for Manchester United. item.title: Why We Beat TCU
item.description: FORT WORTH, TX - OCTOBER 24: West Virginia Mountaineers quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. (3) runs past Texas Christian University Horned Frogs defensive lineman Koron Hayward (16) during the game between the Texas Christian University Horned Frogs and the West Virginia Mountaineers on October 24, 2026 at Amon G. Carter Stadium in Fort Worth, Texas. (Photo by Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images WVU goes on the road and gets a huge win against TCU to bring our record to 5-3 on the season. We enter the bye week with more wins than we had all of last year and some momentum heading into the final 4 games of the season. How did the Mountaineers pull out the first true road win of the year? Let’s get into it… Defense Nobody is going to mistake the WVU defense we saw against TCU with the Steel Curtain, but the fact is that they played a bigger role in getting that win than our offense did. TCU racked up 484 total yards, 29 first downs, and over 37 minutes of possession which is a familiar storyline for our much maligned defense. What was the difference today? We played solid against the run holding TCU to 112 yards rushing 49 of which come on 2 plays. By the time the 4th quarter came along TCU felt pretty one dimensional. Our defense forced TCU to execute on long drives instead of frustrating 2 or 3 play TD drives we have given up over the past 4 games. We still gave up far to many big plays, especially on 3rd down, but we kept everything in front of us, and made TCU prove they could execute consistently on 10 or even 15 play drives, and TCU couldn’t do that consistently without turning the ball over. We forced 3 turnovers, including a strip sack on the final drive that iced the game. As bad as the defense has been this year this is the 2nd week in a row where they got a stop when they had to. Hopefully they can build off this through the bye week. Offense If I had written this immediately following the game, I would have had a hard time saying anything positive about our offense following that game. I felt the play calling was extremely conservative and the offense just simply refused to step on TCU’s throat by taking a 2 score lead anytime our defense got a stop or turnover. Excluding the final defensive stop of the game, the WVU defense forced a punt, missed field goal, or turnover on 5 TCU possessions throughout the game. The WVU offense did not score a single point when they got the ball after those stops. Watching our offense fail to execute our defense did their job time and time again was extremely frustrating, so how can we consider the offense a positive? We still found a way to put up 24 points on the best defense in the Big 12. The TCU hadn’t given up more than 21 points in any game this season. The offense did not have their best day for sure, but they did enough. 24 points against the best defense in the Big 12 is what a bad day for our offense looks like and that says something. Michael Hawkin

item.title: Paul Merson picks surprising Arsenal star performer vs Everton
item.description: Paul Merson picks surprising Arsenal star performer vs Everton Arsenal’s defenders may have been the ones making the headlines after the Gunners’ win over Everton, but Paul Merson picked out Martin Odegaard as his star player. Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images There’s little doubt that Arsenal’s centre-backs had the most eye-catching involvements in the team’s 2-0 win over Everton on Saturday. Other than the fact that they helped the Gunners to a clean sheet, they also scored the two goals. Ezri Konsa netted from close range after a corner, and Gabriel Magalhaes doubled Arsenal’s lead with a header. But Arsenal put in a strong team performance all around, and former Gunner Paul Merson highlighted club captain Martin Odegaard as his best player from the game. Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images “I thought Odegaard was outstanding, if you had to pick someone,” Merson said . “He just ticks it all over, he’s so comfortable, he’s got a great left foot, he’s just a nice, nice player. “When he’s in the mood and he has been in the mood this season, his confidence has been high, he’s been the one for me.” Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images Odegaard was definitely another player who performed very well, completing 89% of his passes including 88% accurate passes in the opposition half, pressing excellently (which was key to Arsenal’s dominance), and taking five shots. Everton were forced into defending very deep throughout the match, and that meant Odegaard’s efforts were often blocked before they could reach the goalkeeper. But it was a strong display from the 27-year-old all the same. Arsenal will need just as many strong performances if they’re going to maintain their current Premier League winning streak at Anfield next weekend. Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images

item.title: Philip Rivers Gets Career News After Shocking Colts Return
item.description: Former Indianapolis Colts QB Philip Rivers was in the running for the head coach job with the Buffalo Bills Getty Philip Rivers shocked the NFL when he returned to the Indianapolis Colts last season. He had been away from the league for half a decade, but when Indy called as injuries ravaged its quarterback room, Rivers answered. Rivers played in three games and couldn’t quite save the Colts’ season, and then he rode off into retirement for a second team. The brief interlude didn’t change the fact that Rivers is a rising mind in the world of football coaching. So far, he has been coaching a high school powerhouse with his son at quarterback, but there’s some expectation when Rivers’ kid moves on to the next level, Rivers might do the same. The latest reporting suggests that could be coming soon. Philip Rivers Coaching News Rivers is expected “to be in the mix” for the newly open North Carolina State head coaching job, according to ESPN’s Pete Thamel. The Wolfpack just fired coach Dave Doeren on Saturday. Rivers played at NC State, and his son Gunnar is a high school senior now committed to play there. The fit would make a ton of sense. Along with the usual crop of coaches and coordinators, a name expected to be in the mix in the NC State process is former star quarterback Philip Rivers. His son, Gunner Rivers, is a highly regarded quarterback recruit committed to play there in Class of 2027. — Pete Thamel (@PeteThamel) October 24, 2026 Rivers was a standout quarterback for the Wolfpack in the early 2000s before being the No. 4 overall pick in the 2004 NFL Draft by the Chargers . He then spent nearly his whole career with the Chargers, only coming to the Colts for the 2020 season before his first retirement — then getting those three games last year with Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson both out due to injury. item.title: PAK vs ENG: Why Pakistan are wearing pink jerseys against England in ODI Tri-series
item.description: Pakistan will wear pink jerseys instead of their usual green kits for their ODI Tri-series match against England at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium on Sunday, October 25. The special jerseys are part of the Pakistan Cricket Board’s (PCB) efforts to raise awareness about breast cancer and encourage people to get checked early. The initiative is being held during October, which is observed worldwide as Breast Cancer Awareness Month. The PCB has teamed up with Pink Ribbon Breast Cancer Trust Hospital to spread awareness and support patients who need treatment. Pakistan, England join hands for breast bancer awareness Pakistan’s players will wear specially designed pink jerseys, while England players, match officials and commentators will wear pink ribbons to show their support. The stumps will also be pink, and stadium screens and advertising boards will carry messages about breast cancer awareness. The PCB has also arranged free breast cancer screenings for fans from October 24 to 26 through its partnership with Pink Ribbon Breast Cancer Trust Hospital. “The Pakistan Cricket Board recognises the responsibility that comes with the immense following and influence of cricket in our country,” said the PCB COO Sumair Ahmad Syed. “Through this Pink Ribbon initiative, we want to use the platform of international cricket to raise awareness about breast cancer and highlight the importance of early detection and timely medical attention.” Fans can also purchase special pink-themed merchandise through the PCB’s online store. Money raised from the initiative will help pay for the treatment of patients who cannot afford it. The board has also arranged an auction of signed jerseys from Pakistan stars Shaheen Afridi and Babar Azam, with proceeds going towards the same cause. Pakistan previously held a Pink Day during their T20I series against South Africa last year. Pakistan eye final spot as England fight to stay alive Away from the awareness campaign, the match is important for both teams in the tri-series. Pakistan will aim for their third consecutive victory to secure a place in the final, while England need a win after losing their first two games. England suffered an 87-run defeat against Pakistan in their previous meeting. They also recently endured one of the highest successful run-chases in ODI history, despite Harry Brook scoring a record-breaking double century. 135190552

item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
